name: Arcturus UW-8 'Barracuda'
description:
A supercavitating pistol that fires solid steel darts encased in a gas-generating sabot, creating a bubble envelope around the projectile that reduces water resistance and extends effective range to 30 meters underwater — double the range of conventional underwater weapons. The Barracuda's darts arrive with enough kinetic energy to penetrate diving equipment, underwater vehicle hulls, and the reinforced suits worn by infrastructure workers operating in contaminated water.

Arcturus developed the UW-8 for naval special operations, but the weapon has found extensive use in GLMZ's underwater economy. The city's submerged spaces host smuggling operations, illegal salvage, and clandestine transit networks that conventional law enforcement cannot effectively police. The Barracuda gives underwater operators a decisive range advantage in engagements where 15 additional meters of reach means the difference between firing first and dying first.

The weapon's gas-generating sabot is its most innovative and most dangerous component. The chemical reaction that produces the supercavitation bubble generates hydrogen gas as a byproduct, which means that firing the Barracuda in enclosed submerged spaces builds up an explosive atmosphere. An operator who fires too many rounds in a sealed flooded chamber risks creating a hydrogen pocket that a single spark will detonate. Field operators have learned to count their shots and ventilate between engagements.
legality: Military — restricted to authorized maritime operations
specifications:
projectile: 6mm supercavitating steel dart
capacity: 8 darts
effective range: 30 meters underwater
muzzle velocity: 250 m/s (supercavitating)
weight: 1.1 kg
length: 230mm
warning: Hydrogen gas buildup in enclosed spaces after 4+ rounds
tactical_use: Extended-range underwater combat. The Barracuda provides range superiority in submerged engagements, allowing the operator to engage targets before they can close to conventional underwater weapon range. Critical safety consideration: hydrogen gas accumulation in enclosed submerged spaces limits sustained fire.
cultural_context: The Barracuda has made underwater spaces in GLMZ measurably more dangerous. Before its introduction, underwater combat was limited to speargun range — effectively grappling distance. The 30-meter range of supercavitating darts has turned flooded tunnels into shooting galleries where ambush positions that were previously safe are now kill zones.
story_hooks: A Barracuda was fired in a sealed flooded chamber, and the hydrogen buildup from repeated shots detonated, collapsing a section of submerged infrastructure. The explosion revealed a hidden chamber behind the collapsed wall containing something that predates GLMZ by centuries.

Someone is using Barracudas to systematically kill the divers who patrol GLMZ's water intake systems. The city's water supply is being left unguarded, and whoever is doing it wants access to the intake tunnels for a reason that can't be good.
related_entities: Axiom Systems White Noise Bubble Generator WNB-1

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, hydrodynamic pistol with a distinctly aquatic design philosophy. The Barracuda resembles a scaled-down speargun crossed with military-grade hardware — sleek, purposeful, and engineered for hostile underwater environments. Its profile is aggressive but refined, suggesting precision rather than brutality.
physical_description.dimensions: 230mm length, 45mm width at grip, 65mm height including gas chamber. Barrel extends 120mm forward of the slide.
physical_description.weight_description: Dense and balanced — 1.1 kg feels substantial in a gloved hand without becoming unwieldy. The weight distribution favors the barrel, anchoring the weapon against recoil impulse in water.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced titanium-polymer composite frame with steel barrel assembly. The gas-generating sabot chamber is precision-machined stainless steel with internal corrosion-resistant coatings.
physical_description.finish: Deep matte gunmetal with brushed titanium accents on the slide. The barrel shows a distinctive satin finish to resist salt-water oxidation. All exposed steel surfaces are hardcoat anodized.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary gunmetal gray with brushed silver-titanium accents on the slide and trigger guard. Heat-dispersal vents along the gas chamber are highlighted in navy blue — a practical design choice and manufacturer signature.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer with subtle ribbing for underwater purchase. Treated with a hydrophobic coating that prevents algae growth and maintains grip security even with heavy glove material.
distinctive_features: Gas-generation chamber prominently bulged beneath the barrel — the weapon's most visually distinctive element
Eight-round drum magazine with transparent polycarbonate section showing dart position
Aggressive cooling vents along the gas chamber in a triangular array pattern
Depth-pressure gauge integrated into the left side of the slide (thin circular window)
Suppression port at muzzle with five radial chambers designed to direct supercavitation bubble formation
Safety lever with three positions: SAFE, FIRE, VENT (hydrogen release)
Weapon rail on underside for tactical light or rangefinder attachment
Corrosion-resistant serial plate engraved on gas chamber showing manufacturing batch and pressure rating
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS logo stamped on the slide in raised lettering. Serial number and pressure certification (max depth 500m) engraved on the gas chamber. Small ⚠ symbol next to the VENT safety position.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field weapons show salt residue buildup around vents and minor scoring on the barrel from repeated supercavitating discharge. Well-maintained examples display evidence of regular chemical treatment. Combat-worn examples show chipped paint on edges and micro-corrosion around the trigger assembly — signs of extended submersion operations.

image_prompt: Product photography of the Arcturus UW-8 Barracuda underwater pistol. Weapon displayed on a dark metallic surface with water droplets and salt residue. Dramatic side-lighting from a cool blue-white source creates sharp shadows across the gas-generation chamber and suppression port. Titanium and gunmetal surfaces catch the light with gunmetal and silver highlights. Close-up detail showing the transparent magazine drum with visible dart positioning. Background is deep navy fading to black, suggesting underwater depth. The weapon is crisp and in-focus, emphasizing precision engineering and corrosion-resistant materials. Cyberpunk GLMZ aesthetic: military-industrial design language, advanced materials, purpose-built lethality. Atmospheric: small air bubbles visible in the water droplets on the surface around the weapon. --ar 3:2 --v 6
